decision.about: how items.json's 102 catalogued layouts become real children so browse() can draw them

options.say: a top-level `await fetch(items.json)` in page.js, unchanged file, so the module's own evaluation waits once and every catalogued item becomes a real BrowseItem child before new Page({...}) runs

decision.because: items.json has to stay byte-identical and fetchable by url (/layouts/doc/studies/approved/page.js fetches it directly, outside this task's fence) — a twin file risks drifting out of sync on the next rebuild; the router already awaits this module's own import(), so a top-level await costs nothing new and removes the old route()/heading-correction race entirely instead of adding a second data file
decision.rule: less is more; no build step

log.msg: BUILT: page.js rebuilt on this.browse() — every items.json entry is a real declared BrowseItem(Page) child; Page's own .name/.url are reserved for the item's own /layouts/browse/<id>/ address, so the entry's OWN name/url fields are renamed to title/real_url on the way in (a real, non-obvious collision, not just a rename for style).

SEAM added to ext/framework/ext/catalog/browse.js (2 small, additive changes, both backward-compatible - verified byte-identical rendering for every existing caller that omits the new option): (1) `rail: false` option skips the sticky search/facets rail entirely, for a caller with its own filter UI; (2) every band heading now carries `data-band="<group>"` unconditionally, so a caller can scroll straight to one band. Documented in ext/catalog/readme.md and doc/method/browse.md.

VERDICT KEYSPACE merged: vkey(item) = item.wire ? item.id : (item.real_url ?? item.url) - used everywhere a verdict is read or written (card mark, strip counts, item verdict line, history, press). Proven live: pressing Approve on a card whose real_url is /layouts/doc/studies/approved/ wrote {item:"/layouts/doc/studies/approved/"} to verdicts.jsonl, and /layouts/doc/studies/approved/page.js (untouched) picked it up into its own Library section with no code change there. Pressing Approve on a wire item (layout-1-flow) wrote {item:"layout-1-flow"} - its short id, as decided.

FOUND, OUTSIDE THIS TASK'S FENCE, NOT FIXED: /layouts/doc/studies/approved/page.js's library_card() assumes every non-wire browse item has a jpeg at /layouts/browse/shots/<id>-1920.jpg. The 5 approved-badge items (id starting approved-*) use items.json's own `shot` field pointing elsewhere instead, so their thumbnail 404s on that page once a verdict is cast on one (confirmed live, console: one 404, page still renders and lists the right title/link). Pre-existing - the same 404 would fire the exact same way if the owner approved one of those 5 from the page's OWN ext/Ask corner control, unrelated to this task's changes. Fix belongs in library_card(), which is outside the fence (not the approved page).

PROOF: private server PORT=8141 (real Windows PID from netstat, not $!). Re-ran all 15 browser-critic checks by number (task.jsonl log lines, browser-critic 2026-09-17) at 400/1280/1920/3440 headless via Playwright, plus the new verdict-by-url checks: 45/45 passed read-only, 48/48 with Approve/Improve pressed for real (once each, on two different items: a real page and a wire item) and the approved-library page checked. Zero console errors at any width. verdicts.jsonl copied then restored to its exact prior state (absent - it 404'd before and after; the owner is the only writer).

LINES: page.js 646 -> 624 (-22, -3.4%); browse.css 297 -> 280 (-17); ext/catalog/browse.js +14 (the seam, shared infrastructure). Real number is well under the study's 300-400 estimate - the study costed deleting the old grid, not the adapter layer a cross-realm catalogue actually needs (BrowseItem's field-renaming) or task 2's vkey merge, both landed in the same file. In exchange: the async DATA/route()/heading-correction race is gone entirely (this page's items are real children now, known synchronously), and the wall is provably the same code path as core/Layout/ and framework/ui/'s own walls instead of a fourth independent copy.

DOCS: readme.md (intro count de-hardcoded, two stale watch-outs fixed, two new ones added), doc/decisions.md (new section: the browse() move + the verdict-keyspace merge, in full, plus the two items.json entries sharing a url disclosed and the out-of-fence 404 named), doc/inventory.md (the id/url field table corrected - url is now the verdict key for everything but the twelve wire items). ext/catalog/readme.md + doc/method/browse.md document the new rail:false option and data-band attribute. assign.outcome:
**`/layouts/browse/` now draws on `this.browse()`, and its verdicts share one trail with `ext/Ask`'s own corner control, keyed by url.**

Every one of the 102 catalogued layouts is now a real declared child (`BrowseItem`) instead of a name `route()` claimed once a fetch resolved — which is what let the hand-rolled 644-line card wall and tier-strip grid come out, replaced by one call to core's own `this.browse()` (the same method `core/Layout/` and `framework/ui/` already stand on). `ext/catalog/browse.js` gained a two-line seam for it: `rail: false` (this page keeps its own sticky tier strip instead of `browse()`'s search-and-facets rail) and `data-band` on every band heading (so that strip can still scroll to one).

The mastermind's `verdict-keyspace` decision also landed: a card now reads and writes its verdict keyed by the real page's own url (`vkey(item)`), the same key `ext/Ask`'s corner control already writes — proven live, an Approve pressed on the browser showed up in `/layouts/doc/studies/approved/page.js`'s own "library" section with **no code change there**. The twelve wire-only items (no real page of their own) keep their short id, as decided.

**Lines: `page.js` 646 → 624 (-22), `browse.css` 297 → 280 (-17).** Smaller than the study's 300–400 estimate, reported honestly rather than forced — the study costed deleting the old grid, not the adapter a cross-realm catalogue needs, or task 2's merge, both landed in this same file. In exchange: the old async-data race (`route()` + a heading-correction hack) is gone entirely, and this page now shares its wall's own code with two others instead of running a fourth copy.

**Proof:** 45/45 read-only checks passed (the browser-critic's 15 findings, re-run at 400/1280/1920/3440, headless, private server), 48/48 with Approve and Improve each pressed once for real — one on a real page, one on a wire item — zero console errors throughout, `verdicts.jsonl` copied then restored to its exact prior (absent) state.

**Left, out of this task's fence:** `/layouts/doc/studies/approved/page.js`'s own `library_card()` 404s a thumbnail for the five `approved-*` items (it assumes a jpeg this page never took) — pre-existing, not caused by this merge, and the fix belongs in that file.
